programme: No coherent programme unites this set. The twelve factors belong to at least six unrelated regulatory families with non-overlapping target logic: a Hippo effector (TEAD2, TP53/EGFR/PAX3), a Polycomb-like repressor (L3MBTL1, RUNX1/CCNE1/MYC), a hematopoietic/megakaryocyte ETS factor (FLI1, GP9/ITGA2B/GP6/GP1BA/MPL/KLF1), an NF-kB coregulator (BCL3, RELA/NFKB1/IL6/TNF/IL23A), the core circadian loop (NPAS2, BMAL1/CRY1/CRY2/PER1/PER2), a PML-body senescence node (PML, TP53/BAX/CASP3/CDKN1A), a forkhead tied to Notch ligands in vasculature (FOXC1, DLL4/DLL1/HEY2/NOTCH1), a luminal-epithelial ETS factor (ELF5, KLK3/FOXA1/STAT5A), a basal Pol III transcription factor with a scattershot target list (GTF3A, VEGFA/TNF/SCN5A/LCT), a T-lineage chromatin organizer (SATB1, IL2/IL4/GATA3), the canonical Notch effector (RBPJ, HES1/NOTCH1/NOTCH3/FOXP3), and a cardiac-conduction homeobox factor (IRX3, GJA1/GJA5/KCND2). No two or three of these share a target vocabulary that would let a reader name a single complex or pathway carrying the concordance.
role_in_a: Not answerable at the module level: individual factors touch disparate processes in kidney/RCC biology (FLI1 in vascular/hematopoietic gene control, PML in clear-cell senescence, ELF5 in angiogenesis suppression, FOXC1/IRX3 mentioned alongside SGLT2 biology) with no evidence these form one axis specific to the papillary subtype.
role_in_b: Not answerable at the module level: none of the twelve factors has a recorded Open Targets association with psoriasis, and no retrieved paper places any of them in psoriatic skin, immune, or keratinocyte biology.
shared_axis: None can be proposed responsibly. A pairing built from factors this heterogeneous, most with zero disease-specific literature and no Open Targets signal in either disease, would be an invented mechanism rather than a read of the evidence.
reasoning: The factors span at least six unrelated regulatory families with no shared target logic, so no module can be named from them as a set; picking a plausible-sounding subset (e.g. RBPJ+FOXC1 as 'Notch') would mean quietly discarding the other ten and building a story the record does not support. Literature support is essentially absent or off-target (clear-cell not papillary, general RCC not subtype-specific, or explicitly flagged as unjudgeable), and no factor has an Open Targets hit in psoriasis at all.
support: PMID 38730056 — places PML in clear-cell (not papillary) renal cell carcinoma via p53/senescence restraint, so it does not establish PML in the disease actually being compared; PMID 40020263 — an SGLT2-biomarker paper in papillary RCC that mentions FOXC1 and IRX3, but not as characterized regulators of a shared programme; PMID 37980532 — places ELF5 in renal cell carcinoma angiogenesis generally, again without papillary-subtype or psoriasis specificity. None of these three, singly or together, supports a shared axis between the two diseases.
how_to_falsify: Take the two factors with the strongest concordance and largest target overlap with an immune or Notch signature, RBPJ and FOXC1, and test in matched papillary RCC tubular-epithelial and psoriatic keratinocyte lines whether perturbing either one coordinately shifts its annotated targets (HES1/NOTCH1/NOTCH3/HEY1/HEY2 for RBPJ; DLL4/DLL1/HEY2/NOTCH1 for FOXC1) in both tissues in the same direction; if no coordinated, tissue-crossing effect is seen, that confirms the concordance reflects network-inference topology rather than a shared regulatory module, consistent with the incoherent call here.
caveats: 112 patient-group comparisons rest on only 2 independent cohort pairs, so the comparisons are not 112 independent replications and apparent concordance counts should be read with that inflation in mind. Kidney and skin are unrelated tissues, and none of the twelve factors carries an Open Targets association with psoriasis at all; for Kidney_Papillary_Cell_Carcinoma, several associations exist but the matching papers found (PML, ELF5) are about clear-cell RCC or RCC in general, not the papillary subtype. The single-view exclusions (THAP7, ZBTB20, TRIB3, etc.) confirm the top per-group hits were filtered out correctly, and no tissue-generic master regulator was excluded here that would otherwise have been reached for — the heterogeneity is native to the surviving list, not an artifact of the exclusion step.
